name: tty
description: Terminal detection and information. Use these functions to check if standard streams are connected to a terminal (TTY) and to get terminal dimensions. Useful for writing CLI tools that behave differently when piped vs interactive. @example tty::is_stdout if { term::Green print } "output" print tty::is_stdout if { term::Reset print } nl

functions.name: height
functions.description: Get terminal height in rows. Returns 0 if not a terminal or size cannot be determined.

functions.name: is_stderr
functions.description: Check if stderr is connected to a terminal (TTY). Returns 1 if stderr is a TTY, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: is_stdin
functions.description: Check if stdin is connected to a terminal (TTY). Returns 1 if stdin is a TTY, 0 otherwise. Useful for detecting if input is from keyboard vs pipe.

functions.name: is_stdout
functions.description: Check if stdout is connected to a terminal (TTY). Returns 1 if stdout is a TTY, 0 otherwise. Useful for disabling colors when output is piped.
examples: tty::is_stdout if { term::Green print } "PASS" print tty::is_stdout if { term::Reset print }

functions.name: size
functions.description: Get terminal dimensions (rows and columns). Returns 0 for both values if not a terminal or size cannot be determined. Tries stdout, stderr, stdin in order, then falls back to LINES/COLUMNS environment variables.
examples: tty::size -> cols drop // just get cols

functions.name: width
functions.description: Get terminal width in columns. Returns 0 if not a terminal or size cannot be determined.
